author: orchestrator
content: Developer rejected plan v1: Plan v1 is rejected: the criteria do not enforce two of its own requirements, so validation could record a pass while the defect this task exists to fix is still in the tree. Keep requirements 1-8, files_to_modify and files_to_create exactly as they are; they are correct. Tighten the acceptance criteria as follows. (1) Requirement 3 demands the constitution section be labelled with CONSTITUTION_RELATIVE, and no criterion settles it: a reconciliation that resolves through constitution_path() but labels the heading with the absolute exported path passes all nine criteria. Add a case that exports ORCHESTRATOR_CONSTITUTION to a readable fixture outside the repo and asserts stdout carries the relative .ai/constitution.md label rather than the exported absolute path, and name that test in the AC-3 verify command. (2) AC-4 cannot settle the first half of its own statement. run_validation_check passes no env= to subprocess.run, so an acceptance criterion inherits the orchestrator environment, which never has ORCHESTRATOR_TASK_DIR set; unittest -v test_hook_resilience therefore passes with the run_hook inheritance bug of requirement 6 fully intact. Add a test that patches hostile ambient values into os.environ, with ORCHESTRATOR_TASK_DIR pointing at a decoy directory that contains valid implementation notes and a valid context block, and asserts a fixture-based case still resolves to its own tmpdir; name that test in its own material criterion so requirement 6 is independently enforced. (3) AC-5 claims no conflict syntax but py_compile only rejects markers that are syntax errors; a marker line inside a docstring or comment compiles cleanly. Append a scan to the AC-5 verify command that reads both hooks and exits non-zero if any line starts with a conflict marker prefix. (4) AC-1 can pass with the TASK-008 half reverted: under cwd resolution the fixture task directory is not found, implementation.md is missing, and the guard still exits 2 for an unrelated reason. Tighten AC-1 so the cwd tree holds complete decodable evidence and the diagnostic must name the undecodable artifact at the exported path, so a cwd-resolving regression fails on the message rather than passing on the exit code. (5) AC-2 relies on the emit() guarantee being carried by a source-level test inside the AC-4 module run, because a UTF-8 validation locale encodes a non-cp1252 blackboard fine. Either force a cp1252 stdout codec in the new AC-2 test subprocess so the criterion stands alone, or state in AC-2 that the explicit-encoding half is carried by that named source-level test. Do not widen the change: still exactly three files modified, none created, and _support.py untouched. The developer answers to Q-1 and Q-2 stand unchanged.

author: implementer
content: Both hook conflicts are reconciled and every new test was checked for discrimination by reverting each half in turn and observing the failure, then restoring it: task_directory->cwd makes AC-1 exit 0 (not a spurious block, which is what ctx-001 item 4 asked for); read_guarded->bare read_text makes AC-1 exit 1 (the silent-failure code); emit->sys.stdout.write makes AC-2 raise UnicodeEncodeError, and it still does so under a UTF-8 ambient locale because AC-2 forces PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252 in the child, which settles ctx-001 item 5; CONSTITUTION_RELATIVE->constitution leaks the absolute temp path into the heading; read_or_warn->bare read_text on the constitution fails both AC-3 and the existing source-level helper count. AC-1 fails on both reverts with distinguishable symptoms, which is what makes it an interaction test rather than two half-tests.

author: implementer
content: The run_hook inheritance defect of requirement 6 is not confined to test_hook_resilience.py. Running the full suite from inside an orchestrated worker session, where the ORCHESTRATOR_* rooting variables are exported, fails six tests in three modules this task does not declare: test_plan_authorization.DeclaredInfrastructureTests (3), test_context_bus.HookBehaviourTests (2), and test_hardening.PreToolUseWriteTests.test_denies_editing_the_hooks_themselves (1). Cause isolated rather than assumed: starting from a cleared environment, exporting ORCHESTRATOR_TASK_DIR alone flips the two test_context_bus cases, and exporting ORCHESTRATOR_REPO_ROOT alone flips them too, so those fixtures inherit ambient rooting and the hooks they invoke read the live task tree instead of the fixture tree. With the five ORCHESTRATOR_* variables cleared the full suite is 777 discovered, all OK. The exported-path preference is main's TASK-008 behaviour, not something this reconciliation introduced. I did not touch those modules because they are outside files_to_modify; a follow-up task should apply the same run_hook fix to them. Note I could not compare against the pre-merge baseline tree: its hooks do not parse at all, so no before/after run is meaningful and the isolation above is the evidence.

author: implementer
content: Two environment facts worth not rediscovering. First, bare `python` on this Windows host is the Microsoft Store App Execution Alias shim and exits 49 with an install prompt; `py -3` (3.13.15) is the working launcher, so every command in this task's notes was run through it. Second, the merge is left unstaged on purpose: both hooks are still UU in the index and the single merge commit is the developer's, per the plan constraint that no intermediate commit with unparsable hooks enters history. The working-tree bytes are the reconciled result, which is what the baseline delta compares against, so validation does not need the index resolved.
